data.title: Salvianolic Acid B Enhances Motor Function Recovery after Spinal Cord Injury in Association with AKT/mTOR/HIF-1α Pathway Activation and Angiogenesis.
data.authors: Yao J; Chen Yingfeng; Pan F; Zhang S

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Salvianolic acid B improved motor recovery, neuronal survival and angiogenesis after rat spinal cord injury in association with AKT/mTOR/HIF-1α activation; the effects were reversed by the AKT inhibitor capivasertib.
data.abstract_excerpt: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a devastating condition with limited treatment options. Salvianolic acid B (SalB), a natural compound from Salvia miltiorrhiza, shows therapeutic potential but its mechanisms in SCI remain unclear. This study combined network pharmacology, molecular docking and in vivo experiments using a rat SCI model, applying the AKT inhibitor capivasertib (AZD5363) for mechanistic verification. Network analysis identified 188 SalB-SCI common targets primarily in the AKT pathway, and molecular docking predicted strong binding between SalB and AKT1.

extracted_findings.intervention: Salvianolic acid B; capivasertib (AZD5363) as AKT inhibitor control
extracted_findings.effect: Improved motor function, reduced tissue damage, enhanced neuronal survival and angiogenesis; abolished by AKT inhibition
